items.title: The issue that cost Pierre Gasly a potential "win" at F1's Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Pierre Gasly reckons he potentially had the pace to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix, had a cooling issue not affected his Alpine Formula 1 car in the closing stages. The Frenchman finished fifth from eighth on the grid, but after 31 of the scheduled 50 laps, Gasly was third behind Red Bull’s eventual winner Max Verstappen and Mercedes’ George Russell.

items.title: F1 pundit calls for real consequences at Ferrari: "I'd chuck Ollie Bearman in for a race"
items.summary: After Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton collided for the second time in three races during the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the paddock debate quickly moved past who misjudged Turn 7 and onto a harder question: how can Ferrari actually stop it from happening again?

items.title: Juan Pablo Montoya explains how Red Bull outsmarted Mercedes at F1 Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Mercedes brought the fastest single-lap package to the Las Vegas Strip - newly crowned 2026 world champion Kimi Antonelli topped qualifying before a five-place engine penalty dropped him to sixth, while George Russell lined up alongside polesitter Max Verstappen.

items.title: Isack Hadjar frustrated – What really happened on Red Bull's team radio in Las Vegas
items.summary: Isack Hadjar started Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix from fourth on the grid, and by lap four he had already found himself running second, right behind Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen.

items.title: Max Verstappen jokes last time he won a race like F1 Las Vegas GP it was "Mario Kart"
items.summary: Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen says the last time he won a race like the Las Vegas Grand Prix was when he was playing Mario Kart. The Red Bull driver converted pole position into his 75th grand prix win, and his third in Las Vegas, in a race that featured 352 overtakes and 35 lead changes.

items.title: Laurent Mekies: Keeping his emotions in check is giving Isack Hadjar “lap time”
items.summary: Isack Hadjar left the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix empty-handed after a Lap 26 front wing failure and a post-race 10-second safety car penalty relegated him to 15th, yet Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies saw something far more encouraging on the Strip.

items.title: Guenther Steiner expects Ferrari board to react after Lewis Hamilton-Charles Leclerc clash
items.summary: Former Haas Formula 1 team principal Guenther Steiner believes Ferrari will make changes after Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc clashed again at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Leclerc spun Hamilton around while the pair fought over sixth place around the streets of Las Vegas, only three weeks after another clash at the Mexican Grand Prix.

items.title: Toto Wolff: Las Vegas was “Indy 500, NASCAR and Formula 1 mixed”
items.summary: Even after watching both Mercedes drivers slip off the podium in the final three laps, team principal Toto Wolff left the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix thrilled by the spectacle.

items.title: Max Verstappen reveals he is considering 2027 Daytona 24 Hours entry
items.summary: Ahead of the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Max Verstappen first paid a visit to Daytona. The Dutchman said he was primarily there to film content with Red Bull, but the visit also raises the question of whether he is seriously considering taking part in the Rolex 24, the endurance race held on the road course of Daytona International Speedway.

items.title: Lando Norris: "Looking at the battery more than where I'm going" in Las Vegas
items.summary: McLaren Formula 1 driver Lando Norris says he spent more of the Las Vegas Grand Prix watching his battery than the road ahead, as he recovered from outside the points to second place. The 2025 champion started third but was running 11th by lap 12, with the MCL40 losing out on the Las Vegas street circuit's long straights.

items.title: F1 Qatar GP 2026: start time, schedule and how to watch
items.summary: The Qatar Grand Prix starts at 8 am PT on Sunday, November 29, which is 11 am ET. Formula 1 returns to the Lusail International Circuit for the penultimate race of the 2026 season, with every session live on Apple TV. The full schedule and viewing information are below.

items.title: F1 Qatar GP 2026: UK times, schedule and how to watch
items.summary: The Qatar Grand Prix starts at 4pm UK time on Sunday 29 November. Formula 1 returns to the Lusail International Circuit for the penultimate race of the 2026 season, with every session live on Sky Sports F1. The full UK schedule and viewing information are below.

items.title: F1 2027 grid: Who will be racing and where?
items.summary: The 2027 Formula 1 grid has very much taken shape with all but one spot now confirmed following a rather safe ‘silly season’ that didn’t present much drama. There is only one team - Haas - that is changing its line-up for next season as many potentially enthralling storylines failed to materialise in regards to the 2027 grid. So, here’s a look at the situation.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari’s top-speed deficit was “brutal” at F1 Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Ferrari Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton says the SF-26’s top-speed deficit was exposed as even more “brutal” than he expected on Las Vegas’ long straights.

items.title: Max Verstappen "would rather stay home" but trusts F1's safety guarantees for Middle East races
items.summary: After Formula 1 informed Imola that it would not be needed as a plan B, F1 is now fully committed to concluding the 2026 season in the Middle East. Although F1 has always maintained that it would do "the right thing" if the security situation deteriorated, it views the MotoGP weekend in Qatar as an example of how the final two Grands Prix can go ahead as planned.

items.title: Who slept best last night: Max Verstappen
items.summary: There were 35 overtakes for the lead, they say, in the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Which sounds believable, but isn't even worth checking. Everyone who watched it knows there were a lot. Apparently, 17 of those involved Max Verstappen reclaiming the lead. And the vast majority were against George Russell.

items.title: Who slept worst last night: Charles Leclerc
items.summary: Frederic Vasseur suggested on Saturday evening (Sunday morning in Europe) that, following the Las Vegas Grand Prix, he could essentially deliver the very same dressing-down he had already given his drivers after Mexico. Because Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton had done it again. And, once again, the roles were exactly the same.

items.title: Colton Herta replaced at Hitech to end poor F2 season early
items.summary: Colton Herta will end his torrid time in Formula 2 early by not returning for the final two rounds of the 2026 season following a “mutual agreement” with Hitech. The nine-time IndyCar race winner made the transition to European single-seaters this year as part of his bid to gain an FIA Superlicence that is required to compete in Formula 1.

items.title: Salary dispute holding up Oliver Bearman’s new Haas F1 deal
items.summary: Ferrari protege Oliver Bearman remains the only driver on the Formula 1 grid without a contract for 2027. It is a situation that would have been hard to imagine just a few weeks ago, given that his retention at Haas had been taken for granted since last summer.

items.title: Haas keeps Rafael Camara in F1, ending his 2026 F2 title bid
items.summary: Haas rookie Rafael Camara will see out the season with Haas in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, effectively ending his F2 championship challenge. Camara was confirmed in October as a full-time replacement for Esteban Ocon in 2027, and was fast-tracked into the seat after Ocon's relationship with the US-owned team deteriorated.

items.title: The one aspect of Max Verstappen "outsmarting" Mercedes that left Red Bull speechless
items.summary: Max Verstappen claimed his fourth victory in the last six Formula 1 Grands Prix. This time, the Dutchman won at what is known as an energy-poor circuit, which is noteworthy given that Red Bull Ford Powertrains was still struggling at such venues at the start of this year.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton: ‘Charles Leclerc’s frame of mind cost us a lot of points today’
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton subtly implied Charles Leclerc’s “frame of mind” was to blame for their collision in Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. Hamilton and Leclerc were sixth and seventh on lap 37 of the Nevadan race, only some two seconds adrift of race leader Max Verstappen, when the Monegasque dived down the inside in Turn 7.

items.title: Winners and losers from F1's chaotically extraordinary Las Vegas GP
items.summary: A pack of cars covered by seconds, the top three trading first position as part of 35 lead changes, and drivers trying to figure out the best positioning to be ahead at the finish line on the final lap; The Las Vegas Grand Prix felt like the glitzy, battery-assisted street course version of the Indy 500.

items.title: Isack Hadjar gets penalty after backing up George Russell in Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Isack Hadjar has received a 10-second penalty for driving unnecessarily slowly in Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix – the result of his actions under the safety car.

items.title: Fred Vasseur furious with latest "unprofessional" Ferrari clash: "It's the same speech as Mexico"
items.summary: Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur says Charles Leclerc's contact with Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "unacceptable" and showed "lack of respect for the team", with the Formula 1 team set for fresh crisis talks just three weeks after their spat in Mexico.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton: With #1 driver backing at key points, we could have beaten Kimi Antonelli this season
items.summary: Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton believes he could have beaten Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli in their battle earlier in the season had he been given more support from Ferrari. The Briton was speaking after the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where he had another clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc, which sent him into a spin.

items.title: Isack Hadjar says freak Las Vegas front wing failure is “ruining my fun” after podium run collapses
items.summary: Isack Hadjar spent the opening half of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix racing wheel-to-wheel with Formula 1’s frontrunners - even pressing Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen for the lead. Halfway through the 50-lap race, a freak mechanical failure reduced the rest of his night to lonely damage limitation.

items.title: Charles Leclerc: Ferrari must find fix to 'unacceptable' feud after Lewis Hamilton clash
items.summary: Charles Leclerc ended the Las Vegas with a 10-second penalty for an avoidable collision with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton – and a telling-off from team boss Frederic Vasseur ringing in his ears.

items.title: Charles Leclerc “embarrassed for the team” after costly Las Vegas clash with Lewis Hamilton
items.summary: Ferrari left the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix with seven points, two 10-second time penalties, and a fresh intra-team mess to untangle. Starting 10th and 11th after a painful double Q2 elimination, Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton spent much of Saturday night fighting over the same stretch of road - until their battle boiled over on Lap 38 at the Turns 7–8 chicane.

items.title: “My mistake was to lift” – Why Kimi Antonelli lost power in Las Vegas F1 victory battle
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli has explained the quirky “mistake” that cost him a shot at Formula 1 victory in the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The fastest driver in qualifying, Antonelli was sixth on the grid owing to a five-place drop for an engine change and was the only top-10 starter on mediums rather than softs, which contributed to a further two-position drop on lap one.
